newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions call off meeting with legislators.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions call off meeting with legislators.

text.p: Argentine union chiefs called off a Wednesday meeting with legislators of the governing Peronist Party because government officials planned to attend, CGT union confederation chief Rodrigo Daer said.

"The meeting with the Peronist Party's national council was suspended because we found out that...officials of the national government were going to participate," Daer said, according to the state-owned Telam news agency.
Instead, the meeting, called to discuss the government's controversial plans to make labor laws more flexible, was postponed until next week.
"We want to speak with just the legislators," Daer said.

But top Peronist senator Eduardo Bauz, speaking after news of the meeting's cancellation, said that President Carlos Menem would not be pressured by unions into abandoning his plans for more flexible labor laws.

Arguing that modernizing labor laws is the only way to reduce 17.1 percent unemployment, Menem wants to dismantle union control on collective wage negotiations, swap redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance, make pay partly dependent on the economic climate and bring greater flexibility to working hours.
